text:
Maya: Heads up — running the apples-to-apples replay on the KV prefix cache yesterday showed weird drop-offs in hit rate under concurrent replay traffic. logging + a small repro attached below.
Josh: ugh. is this the new eviction path we merged last week? :eyes:
Maya: I suspect the concurrent eviction + warmup path. Observed windows where many prefixes became unreachable and the hit rate dropped from ~87% -> ~45% for ~12s under a 200c replay.
Ben: can you paste the replay command you used? and dataset size? we need to know if it's synthetic or recorded traffic.
Maya: recorded traces from /replays/customer-x/2026-02-20. Command:
```
./replay_harness --trace customer-x-0220.json \
  --concurrency 200 --batch-policy auto --kv-warmup 1h \
  --measure-prefix-hitrate --out=run-1798765432.log
```
Maya: Important bits: batch-policy auto triggers kernel selection that sometimes switches mid-request when sequence lengths vary. Also we use concurrent eviction threads default=4.
Tamar: did you run with prefix prefetching enabled? that can change warmup dynamics.
Maya: yes prefetch=on. We also tried prefetch=off — still saw transient drops but smaller (87% -> 62%).
Linh: i pulled the flamegraph from the run — there's a big contention spike in the cache mutex around the eviction loop. looks like many workers try to populate the same slot.
Ben: hmm which eviction algorithm? LRU or CLOCK? recent change made CLOCK approximate with background async cleaning.
Maya: CLOCK with async background trimming (merged in PR #682). The trimming task is rate-limited but appears to kick in more aggressively under high concurrency.
perf-bot: [perf-regression] alert: kv_prefix_cache_hitrate_regression detected in run-1798765432 vs baseline-1790001111. delta = -0.22 (p<0.01)
Josh: ok that's concrete. can we reproduce deterministically with a small synthetic generator? maybe create a synthetic trace with controlled prefix reuse and a few long-tails.
Maya: yes i added a small synthetic that stresses same hot prefixes + several mid-tail prefixes. command below:
```
./replay_harness --synth hot=0.6 mid=0.3 tail=0.1 --requests 200000 --concurrency 200
```
Maya: Run shows same pattern. I captured kv logs (attached): several `WARN kv/cache: evicted but in-flight` and `ERROR kv/cache: missing_prefix_fetch_conflict` spikes.
Tamar: "evicted but in-flight" suggests race between fetcher and eviction. Maybe fetch increments refcount then eviction sees 0 because refcount not yet visible due to reorder.
Linh: i looked at the code in cache.cc: when a fetch wins, we do fetch->insert() then notify waiters. eviction acquires the same bucket lock; i think the window is between creating entry and setting the populated flag.
Ben: could be a memory ordering issue on x86? but sounds unlikely. we should add instrumentation: increment counters on creation, populate, eviction, fetch-miss, and record stack for conflicting evictions.
Maya: added lightweight counters and reran. timeline (abridged):
- t0 warmup hitrate climbs to 88%
- t1 eviction-trimmer runs, evicts ~12k entries
- t1+3s fetch storms for some prefixes -> many fetches create placeholder entries
- t1+5s many placeholder entries get evicted before populate -> missing fetches -> cache miss spike
Josh: so placeholders are being scheduled for eviction even though fetch is in progress. should we pin placeholders from eviction until populate completes?
Tamar: yes that's one mitigation. Another is to make eviction skip placeholders that have an active refcount or in-flight flag.
Ben: for correctness we need to ensure in-flight fetches are visible to evictor. a simple fix: set in_flight=true under bucket lock before releasing to fetcher thread.
Linh: i attempted that locally: set flag under lock, then spawn fetch. it reduces the missing-prefix errors but increases memory stew because many placeholders are pinned and increase steady-state memory.
Maya: tradeoff observed: memory usage +6% but hitrate stable at 86% under stress.
Josh: i think +6% memory is acceptable if it prevents 40% hit drop. But we should also look at kernel selection / batching — that mid-request kernel switch might amplify contention by producing more concurrent small KV lookups.
Maya: yes when batch-policy auto flips kernels, we saw sudden increase in small sequence requests that cause more prefix lookups. I instrumented the kernel-switch events; they spike right before the hitrate collapse.
Ben: can we force kernel pinning for experiments? rule: kernel selection only at request start, not mid-request.
Linh: quick patch to avoid mid-request switching dropped the small lookups by ~30% and smoothed the eviction pressure. worth pursuing.
Maya: proposed next steps:
1) short-term: pin in-request kernel (config toggle) + pin placeholders during in-flight fetch (guarded by flag) to avoid missing-prefix churn.
2) medium-term: change eviction to prefer aged clean slots and skip placeholders; tune trimmer rate adaptively using queue depth.
3) longer-term: redesign placeholder lifecycle — allow lightweight async completion without occupying eviction-critical slots.
Josh: i agree. also we should add an apples-to-apples benchmark in CI that runs a 60s 200c replay against a standard trace and asserts hitrate >= 80% and no missing_prefix_fetch_conflict logs.
perf-bot: noted. creating perf CI job: job-id=perf/kv-prefix-stability/1798765432
Tamar: i'll prototype the in-flight flag patch and the config toggle. will push a branch and ask for quick review.
Maya: thanks. attaching two files: run-1798765432.log (kv traces), flamegraph-1798765432.svg, and a short script reproduce.sh
Ben: once branch is up i'll run longer soak (30m) and collect memory profiles + kernel switch histograms.
Linh: FYI i also ran a microbench of the eviction lock with 32 threads. shows ~4x increase in waiters during the hotspot. sharing results in thread.
Maya: great. if anyone wants to triage with me tomorrow 10am PST i can walk through the flamegraphs and logs.
Josh: ping me the PR when ready. also add a feature flag for pinning placeholders so we can toggle quickly in Dedicated.
Maya: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Deploy bot: scheduled a canary for branch/tamar/kv-inflight-pin on dedicated-canary at 2026-03-22T18:00:00Z
Maya: added the canary to the thread. we'll monitor hitrate and the perf CI job.
Ben: noted. really appreciate the detailed repro — made debugging much faster.
